description: Given Dagster resources holding credentials (ConfigurableResource subclasses, EnvVar, built-in integration resources), map each to the matching Orchestra connection type, referenced by name/${{ ENV.* }} in pipeline YAML — never inlined.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset to an Orchestra pipeline task, focusing on how the SnowflakeResource's credentials should be represented (see files/snowflake_resource_asset.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SNOWFLAKE task whose connection: references either a name_XXXXX connection or a ${{ ENV.* }} variable — never the literal account/user/password from the EnvVar calls. warehouse/database/role are not written as task parameters since they belong to the connection, not duplicated per task unless the source genuinely varies them.

assertions.text: The task uses the SNOWFLAKE integration
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT / SNOWFLAKE_USER / SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env var names are not written as literal parameter values in the YAML

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job to Orchestra pipeline tasks, making sure the two Airbyte resources map to the correct Orchestra connection types (see files/airbyte_cloud_and_server.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sync, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Two tasks: one using an Airbyte Cloud-style connection (from AirbyteCloudResource, API-key auth) and one using an Airbyte Server-style connection (from AirbyteResource(host=,port=), self-hosted), each with the correct connection_id from the source, and neither resource's credentials (AIRBYTE_CLOUD_API_KEY, AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER/PASSWORD) written as literal values.

assertions.text: Both Airbyte tasks are distinguished from each other rather than collapsed into one identical connection type — AirbyteCloudResource and AirbyteResource(host=,port=) map to different Orchestra connections
Connection ids 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 and 66666666-7777-8888-9999-000000000000 are carried over as the sync targets (as parameters, not as the connection: name itself)
AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER and AIRBYTE_SERVER_PASSWORD are not written as literal parameter values

evals.prompt: Convert this task to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how the Snowflake credentials behind the SnowflakeResource injected into the op should reach the running code (see files/rowcount_op.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task whose code reads the Snowflake credentials from the Snowflake connection *linked* on the Python connection — via orchestra.get_linked_connection("snowflake", ...) or the injected <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD> environment variables (e.g. SNOWFLAKE__PROD_12345__SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) — rather than the Snowflake account/user/password being copied into the Python connection's own Secrets or written into the YAML. A deleted or undecryptable linked connection is skipped silently, so the code must not assume the variables are present.

assertions.text: The converted code reads the warehouse credentials from a linked connection — get_linked_connection(...) or an injected SNOWFLAKE__<CONNECTION_ID>__SNOWFLAKE_* environment variable — rather than re-declaring them
No Snowflake account/user/password value is written into the YAML
The existing Snowflake connection is linked on the Python connection instead of its credentials being copied into that connection's Secrets — the warehouse credential stays in one place

Linked-credential environment variables are named <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD>, with a double underscore between parts and the field's ID (e.g. snowflake_password) as the last part — not a single underscore or the field's display label
The code tolerates a linked connection being skipped (deleted or undecryptable credentials) rather than assuming os.environ[...] is set — e.g. .get() or an explicit presence check

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/secrets_manager_resource.py). Note where the credential actually resolves from and tell me how it should reach Orchestra. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SNOWFLAKE task whose connection: is a name_XXXXX or ${{ ENV.* }} reference with no credential inlined. Alongside the YAML, the response recognises that the resource resolves its credential from AWS Secrets Manager and offers the external credential store route — create an Orchestra AWS Secrets Manager connection, then set Credential Store on the Snowflake connection and give it the Secret ARN — instead of asserting the account/user/password must be re-entered by hand. It should not invent credential values, which the source does not contain.

assertions.text: The task uses the SNOWFLAKE integration
No Snowflake credential value is written into the YAML
Recognises that the credential resolves from AWS Secrets Manager at run time, so the Dagster repo holds no account/user/password to extract

Offers the external credential store route — create an Orchestra AWS Secrets Manager connection, then set Credential Store on the Snowflake connection and point it at the Secret ARN — rather than stating flatly that the credential must be re-entered by hand in Orchestra

Notes that the AWS Secrets Manager connection has to exist before AWS Secrets Manager can be chosen as the credential store, and that the secret's value must be a JSON object holding the Snowflake connection's parameters — every required one, not only the password

Does not invent a preceding task that fetches the secret — AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER has no integration_job, so Credential Store on the connection is the only route, not an AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER task feeding a downstream task
Does not fabricate a Snowflake account, user, or password — the source contains none
